description: A festival director must approve the binding public exhibition package for an immersive short-film installation, including the session format, equipment capacity, rights limits, accessibility setup, and the creator's opening-night appearance.

shared_context.S1: The festival will present the immersive short film 'Tide Memory' in a public installation during its opening weekend.
shared_context.S2: The current draft exhibition plan uses eight stations, 15-minute sessions, unrestricted recording by visitors, and a general accessibility notice.
shared_context.S3: Mara has authority to approve the final exhibition and opening-night package.
shared_context.S4: The festival's standard finalization meeting requires the technical producer, rights counsel, accessibility coordinator, and guest liaison to report any confirmed production requirements before Mara signs the package.

PF1.text: Jonah's equipment test showed that the installation can run reliably on exactly six stations, not eight, and each headset requires a five-minute sanitation reset between sessions; he recorded the test in the technical worksheet after yesterday's systems check, but the worksheet has not yet been attached to the festival master brief.

PF2.text: Leila confirmed with the distributor that the festival license permits exactly three public showings of 'Tide Memory' and prohibits visitor recording; she received the countersigned license addendum this morning, but its limits have not yet been entered in the event contract summary.

PF3.text: Sofia's accessibility review requires exactly two captioned companion tablets and a seated orientation before each session; she completed the review with the access consultant on Tuesday, but the resulting access specification is still in her department's review folder.

PF4.text: Evan confirmed with the creator's agent that the creator can attend only on opening night at exactly 6:30 PM for a 15-minute audience Q&A; the agent confirmed this by email today, but Evan has not yet updated the guest schedule.

acceptance_conditions: The installation must use timed sessions with exactly six stations and 20-minute sessions including the required reset interval.
The festival must limit the installation to exactly three public showings.
The accessibility plan must provide exactly two captioned companion tablets and a seated orientation.
The creator Q&A must occur at exactly 6:30 PM on opening night and last exactly 15 minutes.
The technical operating requirement, rights restriction, accessibility specification, and creator schedule must each be logged as commitments.
Mara must cite Sofia's spoken accessibility finding in the justification.

content_checks.C5: decisions['accessibility_plan'] == 'two captioned tablets and seated orientation'
content_checks.C7: any(c['type'] == 'technical_operations' and c['target'] == 'Tide Memory' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C8: any(c['type'] == 'rights_compliance' and c['target'] == 'Tide Memory' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C9: any(c['type'] == 'accessibility_setup' and c['target'] == 'Tide Memory' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C10: any(c['type'] == 'creator_appearance' and c['target'] == 'Tide Memory' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The equipment test changes the draft from eight stations and 15-minute sessions to exactly six stations and 20-minute timed sessions, and requires the technical-operations commitment.
The countersigned license changes the permitted exhibition count to exactly three and changes visitor recording from allowed to prohibited, requiring the rights-compliance commitment.

The accessibility review changes the general notice into exactly two captioned companion tablets plus a seated orientation and requires Sofia's finding to be cited in addition to the accessibility commitment.
The agent email fixes the creator appearance at exactly 6:30 PM for exactly 15 minutes and requires the creator-appearance commitment.
